issue.title: reportRepo.create fails with "date/time field value out of range"
issue.body:
Our script creates one report per client per month through
`POST /api/v1/reports`. A bug on our side made it ask for February 2027 with
`"to": "2027-02-29"`, and the API answered `500 internal error`. The log line:

    {"level":"error","msg":"unhandled error","err":{"type":"DatabaseError","code":"22008","message":"date/time field value out of range: \"2027-02-29\"","stack":"error: date/time field value out of range: \"2027-02-29\"\n    at /srv/ledgerline/node_modules/pg/lib/client.js:535:17\n    at async Object.query (/srv/ledgerline/src/db/client.ts:27:22)\n    at async Object.one (/srv/ledgerline/src/db/client.ts:39:18)\n    at async Object.create (/srv/ledgerline/src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts:81:17)"}}

So the INSERT in `src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts` passes the dates in as plain
strings and Postgres chokes on them; `"to": "2026-04-31"` does the same. The
date was our mistake, but it should get a 400 that names the field, not a 500.

input.title: Reject impossible calendar dates in report from/to with a 400
input.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

The `isoDate` schema only checks the shape `YYYY-MM-DD` with a regex, so values like 2027-02-29 or 2026-04-31 pass validation and reach the INSERT in reportRepo.create, where Postgres raises 22008 and the API returns a 500. Add a refinement to `isoDate` that parses the string and confirms it round-trips to the same year, month and day (e.g. via Date.UTC and comparing components), with a message like "not a valid calendar date". Because `from` and `to` use isoDate in both createSchema and updateSchema, the zod error will become a 400 naming the field for POST and PATCH.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The `isoDate` validator in `src/api/reports.ts` only checks the `YYYY-MM-DD` shape with a regex. Impossible dates such as 2027-02-29 and 2026-04-31 pass it, reach the INSERT in `reportRepo.create`, and Postgres rejects them, which surfaces as a 500. `reportRepo.ts` is only where the error appears, because it passes the already-validated values through. The fix is to make `isoDate` check that the date really exists, so `from` and `to` return a 400 that names the field. `src/api/errors.ts` already turns a ZodError into a 400 whose `details` name the failing field. Draft PR: pr-7.
